editions.text: The station logged 233 feeder visits and 20 species, running slightly above the recent weekly average of 217 visits. All twelve species observed visually have appeared at the station on at least five of the last seven days. Tufted Titmice led the visual count with 113 visits. The day began with a Tufted Titmouse twelve minutes before sunrise and ended with a Northern Cardinal fourteen minutes after sunset. No new species were recorded, and the absence of Northern House Wrens, Northern Flickers, and Pileated Woodpeckers keeps the diversity near the week’s median.

A Tufted Titmouse took the platform feeder twelve minutes before sunrise. By 09:00, small songbirds had claimed the perch, with fifty visits recorded compared to thirteen for Carolina Chickadees. Carolina Wrens accounted for twenty-five detections in the 09:00 hour, and a solitary American Crow passed through at 08:26.

One hundred feeder visits were logged by 10:30.

111 feeder visits logged by 15:56, below the recent seven-day average of nearly 190. Tufted Titmice hold 59 confident visits, while Carolina Chickadees hold 14. A Broad-winged Hawk was detected at 13:00.

Carolina Wrens have 46 detections, and American Crows have 45. The afternoon air holds a high of 29.2°C with light wind and trace precipitation.

A House Finch is seen at a ground-level treat bowl, bringing the confident House Finch total to four. An adult female Northern Cardinal perches on the seed feeder in the grassy backyard, bringing her total to ten.
